subject: Hosting scoping checklist and cutover preferences
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@fintechcorp.com>; Daniel Cho <dan.cho@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-18T15:12:00Z
Subject: Hosting scoping checklist and cutover preferences

Hi Alice / Dan —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and a short scoping checklist so we can lock down the recommended hosting approach (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC) and draft a targeted SOW. I captured the items we discussed and a few clarifying questions below. I've attached the scoping checklist PDF for reference.

High-level recap (what we observed on the call):
- Primary need: production inference for customer-facing personalization and scoring (low-latency).
- Current setup: mostly using OpenAI APIs for experimentation; small self-hosted batch cluster for internal models.
- Key constraints: EU data residency, PCI-adjacent data, and procurement timeline in Feb.

Questions / info we still need to recommend a deployment mode and rough sizing:
1) Data residency & isolation: do logs/traces that include PII need to remain in customer VPC only, or can token logs be stored in Redwood-managed EU region for 30 days?
2) Throughput targets: please confirm expected QPS (avg / peak) and concurrent sessions and a target p50/p95 latency.
3) Migration origin: will you cut traffic from OpenAI API directly to our endpoint, or do you prefer a phased approach (canary routing + gradual prefix caching)? Any existing on-prem GPU pool to decommission?
4) Security/attestation: procurement requested SOC2 and network diagrams — Ben, I cc'd you to attach the SOC2 summary and an example topology.
5) Budget / contract shape: do you have a preferred pricing model (usage-first) or commit / reserved capacity range we should aim for when drafting the quote?

Suggested next steps:
- Customer: answer the three bullets above (residency, QPS, migration plan).
- Redwood: Ben to propose an initial deployment topology (Hosted->Dedicated->Private options) and a runbook for phased cutover.
- Schedule a 60-minute technical design review with your infra team (please propose times for Jan 25–27).

I'll follow up with a first-draft topology and SOW template once we have the QPS and residency answers.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
E: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai | M: +1 415-555-0132
[Attachment: 20270118-hosting-scoping-checklist.pdf (pdf)]

From: Alice Park <alice.park@fintechcorp.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Cho <dan.cho@fintechcorp.com>, procurement@fintechcorp.com
Date: 2027-01-18T18:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosting scoping checklist and cutover preferences

Evelyn — thanks for the clear recap and checklist. A few answers from our side to help you size and recommend:

1) Residency & logs: All production tokens and any telemetry that could be considered PCI-adjacent must remain in our EU tenant. We can allow aggregated telemetry out of region but raw token logs must stay in our VPC.

2) Throughput: avg ~40 QPS, typical burst/peak up to 250 QPS for short periods (marketing spikes). Concurrent session count around 900 sessions with ~3.5 second average response windows; our p95 latency target is <200ms end-to-end.

3) Migration plan: we are currently on OpenAI (for most online traffic) and have a small self-hosted GPU pool (K80/GTX class) used for experimental workloads. Procurement wants a low-risk phased migration: start with a small percentage (5–10%) canary traffic, validate correctness and latency, then ramp with rollback policies. We would likely decommission parts of the on-prem cluster after cutover.

4) Security: attaching our security questionnaire (redacted internal fields) and will need SOC2 and network topology from you.

5) Budget / timeline: procurement is targeting an Approved PO in early March. For us to make a clear case internally, we need a 12-month committed option with predictable unit economics (ballpark committed spend range would be helpful).

Can you send a suggested topology and a phased cutover runbook for our infra review? Also propose times for Jan 25–27 for the technical design session.

Thanks — Alice
Alice Park
Head of Product, FinTechCorp
[Attachment: fintech-security-questionnaire.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@fintechcorp.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-19T09:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosting scoping checklist and cutover preferences

Hi Alice — quick technical response with an initial recommendation and sizing notes.

Recommendation summary (short):
- Given EU residency + PCI-adjacent constraints + the need for predictable economics, a Dedicated capacity deployment inside a customer VPC (Private Dedicated) is the lowest-friction option. It gives you reserved throughput, private networking, and control over raw logs. We can also offer a hybrid where critical traffic goes to Private Dedicated and non-sensitive workloads use our Hosted API to lower cost.

Sizing (very rough ballpark; we'll firm up after telemetry traces):
- For avg 40 QPS with 3.5s avg request length and 250 QPS burst, approximate sizing = 8xA10G-class-equivalents with a small autoscale reserve (20%). This supports KV cache warmup and canary phases.

Migration approach (phased):
- Phase 0: prep & network setup (VPC peering, LB, monitoring).
- Phase 1: small canary (5–10% traffic) using prefix-level routing + prefix caching warmed via synthetic requests. Validate outputs and latency SLA.
- Phase 2: ramp to 50% and run dual-write logging (store tokens in customer VPC).
- Phase 3: full cutover and decommission on-prem GPUs.

Operational notes:
- We support model fallbacks (OpenAI) as a cost/backstop path and can route by policy.
- We'll provide a runbook template (SRE playbook) with rollback triggers and latency/error thresholds.
- SOC2 summary attached and a proposed topology drawing.

Attachments included: SOC2-summary.pdf, proposed-topology-v1.png, runbook-template-v0.1.md (stub).

If this approach sounds right, we can draft a committed capacity quote (12 month) that maps to the sizing above.

Best —
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SOC2-summary.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: proposed-topology-v1.png (png)]
